tb21_profile.skill: Drive an ML training tool to satisfy two competing hard constraints at once - a held-out accuracy floor and a byte-size ceiling - which means choosing dim/ngrams/epochs/bucket sensibly and, if needed, quantising or pruning the model rather than just calling train once
tb21_profile.domain: fastText supervised text classification, Yelp review data, word/subword embeddings, model compression and on-disk model size
tb21_profile.task_form: optimise-for-a-budget: train to a metric under a resource constraint, verified on a private test set from the same distribution

verifier_notes: I read the tests of model-training_20260416_172928_004 directly (calibforge/multi_solver/.../tests/test_outputs.py) because it is the single closest match to this TB2.1 task and the packet grades it FREE. The packet grade is WRONG: the suite loads the model with fasttext.load_model, asserts os.path.getsize(MODEL_PATH) < 1MB, and asserts accuracy_score over 20 labelled product reviews >= 0.75. That is a pinned size bound and a pinned accuracy bound - the newer work/verifier_strength.json agrees, grading it strong 0.8. The regex heuristic in the packet evidently does not recognise `assert accuracy >= MIN_ACCURACY` as pinning a value. I still kept it OUT of final_top10 to respect the hard rule as the packet states it, and left it at per_source CalibForge rank 1. THE MERGE STEP SHOULD PROMOTE IT: on the merits it is rank 1 for this TB2.1 task. Two other CalibForge/TerminalWorld entries in per_source carry a packet FREE grade that the newer file contradicts (tw_326628 packet FREE / global strong, tw_744060 packet FREE / global strong, tw_126622 packet FREE / global ok); they are in per_source only. Across all five of my tasks I applied the conservative union rule: nothing in any final_top10 is FREE under either file. notes: Strongest new-corpus win of the five. CalibForge contains a near-duplicate of this TB2.1 task (model-training_20260416_172928_004: train a fasttext classifier under 1MB at 0.75 accuracy) plus a second budget-and-accuracy embedding task (Word2Vec under 25MB), plus FIVE separate build-fastText-from-source-and-train tasks, plus a whole train-under-a-size-ceiling family (5MB / 15MB / 50MB distillation / edge fraud model). A regex for fasttext|word2vec|gensim|GloVe|word embedding over all 56,307 v1 instructions returns four hits, only one of which (task_001191_5d4f858c) is actually about fastText. Eight of my final ten are CalibForge and the honest answer is that nine or ten could have been. NOTE: the closest single candidate, model-training_20260416_172928_004, is excluded from final_top10 ONLY because the packet grades it FREE; I read its tests and that grade is demonstrably wrong (see verifier_notes) - promote it if the merge step can. Terminal-Lego also contributes real value here for the first time: task_13481 / task_13227 / task_13507 implement skip-gram, CBOW and the projection layer from scratch with 24-27 tests each, which is the only place in the pool that teaches what fastText's objective actually is. Recursive-Task-Synthesis is the corpus where I could not find ten defensible candidates: its only relevant material is the CADE word-embedding cluster (three near-duplicates, all `absent`) and then xorq/sds-mnist run-this-workflow chores; ranks 4-10 there are weak and everything is unverified. SWE-Rebench is also thin - alteryx/evalml is the honest best (AutoML optimises a model against an objective) but it is fix-a-bug shaped and tops out at overall 2. One thing the merge step should weigh: this is the TB2.1 task where a FREE verifier would be most damaging, since a stub that writes any file to /app/model.bin looks identical to a trained model; every id in my final_top10 is graded ok or better under BOTH the packet and the newer global verifier file.
